name: Missouri Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: BBQ, Toasted Ravs & Custard
description:
Missouri's restaurants, from Kansas City burnt ends to toasted ravioli on St. Louis's Hill and Springfield cashew chicken.

Missouri Eats is a free guide to eating in Missouri: 7 Kansas City barbecue joints, 6 toasted ravioli tables on The Hill, 8 St. Louis classics and 12 stops on Springfield's Cashew Chicken Trail we checked by hand, plus 12,766 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 629 towns, from Kansas City and St. Louis to Springfield, Columbia and the Bootheel. No account, no ads.

MISSOURI GUIDES
• Kansas City Barbecue: from Arthur Bryant's by 18th and Vine to Jack Stack at the Freight House.
• Toasted Ravioli: Charlie Gitto's, Rigazzi's and more on The Hill.
• St. Louis Classics: slingers, St. Paul sandwiches, Provel pizza and Ted Drewes frozen custard.
• Springfield Cashew Chicken: stops on the Springfield CVB's Cashew Chicken Trail.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places, from Gioia's Deli to the J. Huston Tavern (1834).

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "burnt ends", "slinger", "cashew chicken".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or a Missouri tourism office's own page. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. "Serves alcohol" comes from the State of Missouri's active by-the-drink licenses (3,811 places); a place without one is unknown, never "no". Missouri has no statewide inspection data, so the app shows no inspection result and links the state health department's food-safety page. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Missouri Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Missouri, its Division of Alcohol and Tobacco Control or any health department), any team or university, or the James Beard Foundation. Alcohol license data is modified from its original source, the State of Missouri, which makes no warranty as to its completeness, accuracy or timeliness. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Missouri Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Missouri (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: Kansas City barbecue, toasted ravioli on St. Louis's Hill, St. Louis classics and Springfield cashew chicken, 34 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard Foundation's honorees. It also lists 12,766 restaurants, cafés and bars in 629 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Kansas City Barbecue (or Toasted Ravioli, St. Louis Classics, Springfield Cashew Chicken, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the Missouri health department's food-safety page in Safari (Missouri publishes no statewide inspection results as data, so none is shown).
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("burnt ends", "slinger", "cashew chicken").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses, the State of Missouri's data disclaimer and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Missouri (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Missouri, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Missouri Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Missouri Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Missouri Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the State of Missouri's active liquor licenses (data.mo.gov, modified for use, with the State's disclaimer quoted in the app; no licensee names are kept); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/missouri-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Missouri; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public government data, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
